intro.objective: Multiply surds using √a × √b = √(ab). Divide surds using √a ÷ √b = √(a/b). Expand brackets involving surds and simplify the result. Recognise the difference of two squares pattern with surds.
commonMistakes: (√3)² = 3, not √9 or 9². The square and the root cancel.
When dividing: √18 ÷ √2 = √(18/2) = √9 = 3. It often becomes a whole number!
methodSteps: Step 1: √a × √b = √(ab) — multiply numbers under the root.
Step 2: √a × √a = a — a surd times itself gives the number.
Step 3: √a ÷ √b = √(a/b) — divide numbers under the root.
Step 4: Expand brackets using FOIL: (a + √b)(c + √d) = ac + a√d + c√b + √b×√d.
Step 5: Simplify — collect like surds and simplify any resulting surds.

questions.content:
Expand and simplify:

   a) (2 + √3)²       b) (√7 − 1)²       c) (3 + √2)(3 − √2)

a) Show that (√a + √b)(√a − √b) = a − b.  (2 marks)

b) Hence simplify (√11 + √3)(√11 − √3).  (2 marks)

A rectangle has length (3 + √5) cm and width (3 − √5) cm.

   a) Find the exact area.  (2 marks)
   b) Find the exact perimeter.  (1 mark)
   c) The area of a different rectangle is 4 cm². The sides are (a + √b) and (a − √b). If b = 5, find a.  (2 marks)
